### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via PageComponentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via PageComponentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via PageComponentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ca7a805ca810bb9eb1c1f6910401f8c582129db` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8295030a50c522f8bf405713c2d18d01d4670aa` — the merge of head `8f64f1ae3484485d9cfc0d1733456cc575aaa11e` into base `1ca7a805ca810bb9eb1c1f6910401f8c582129db`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8295030a50c522f8bf405713c2d18d01d4670aa && git checkout c8295030a50c522f8bf405713c2d18d01d4670aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ca7a805ca810bb9eb1c1f6910401f8c582129db 8f64f1ae3484485d9cfc0d1733456cc575aaa11e && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ca7a805ca810bb9eb1c1f6910401f8c582129db && git merge --no-ff 8f64f1ae3484485d9cfc0d1733456cc575aaa11e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ca7a805ca810bb9eb1c1f6910401f8c582129db
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ca7a805ca810bb9eb1c1f6910401f8c582129db` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f64f1ae3484485d9cfc0d1733456cc575aaa11e`
Local-runs: none

PR #23146 (card #23036; body lines `Fixes #23036`, `Clause-②: no`), judged on the net diff against `main` at merge base `dfb3ba2b2`: 5 files, +261 / −19. Inputs: the card body and its comments 6124818846, 6132762281, 6136306937, 6137432578 and 6137462927; objectui#9308 (ruling B, comment 5651694454) and #17203; the PR body, file list and diff; the check-runs on this head. The cited renderer lines were read in the objectui checkout at the `.objectui-sha` pin `1fb1ced36243`, which this PR does not move. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The spec text writes page state as `page.` followed by a variable name in angle brackets; it is written `page.VAR` below.

### ① Derived judgments

Published surface touched: the `.describe()` of `PageComponentSchema.visibleWhen` (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:678` at the head) and its two republished rows in `content/docs/references/ui/page.mdx` (`:304`, `:443`). The TSDoc above it (`:632`–`:677`) is a source face, judged with the describe because an AI author opening the file reads it.

1. **Mounted-roots sentence — RIGHT.** FROM "additionally mounts `features`, `os.user` and binds `data` to the data-source ADAPTER here" TO "additionally mounts `features` and `os.user` … It mounts NO `data` root here: a `data.*` read faults and a faulting predicate renders the component, so such a gate never gates; the page's row is `record`." At the pin: `react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:665-676` (`configEvaluationScope`) builds `{ ...predicateScope, current_user: predicateScope.user, record (only for a non-array object row), page }`, and the memo builds this surface's evaluator from it at `:1228-1229`; `app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx:181-190` (`buildExpressionScope`) returns `{ current_user, user, ctx: { user }, os: { user }, features }` and nothing else; the only production mount of `PredicateScopeProvider` under `packages/` is `ExpressionProvider.tsx:306` (the one other hit is `packages/react/README.md:87`, documentation). So the mounted set is exactly `record`, `current_user`, `user`, `ctx.user`, `os.user`, `features` and `page` — the union the describe names — and no `data`; `SchemaRenderer.tsx:1194-1206` records the absence as the ruling-B decision. Fail-soft: the production branch at `:1319` calls `evaluateCondition(raw, { onFault })` with no `throwOnError`, `evaluateCondition` (core `ExpressionEvaluator.ts:341` onward) answers a fault with `true`, and the SHOW leg renders on `true`; the ruling's own implementation report measured an absent `data` root as `data is not defined` answered `true`. That is the card's measurement (`data.total` greater than 0 and `data.total == 0` both SHOWN), and the sentence states it.
2. **PLANNED api-binding sentence — RIGHT, and it agrees with `page.zod.ts:502`.** NEW: "`data` is declared only for an element whose `dataSource` is the PLANNED API binding (`provider: 'api'`), which reads its bound value as `data` once that binding's renderer ships." `:502`, unchanged, says "[PLANNED — not yet rendered] … binds the selected value, which the element reads as `data` in its expression holes and its `visibleWhen` … until they ship, the binding parses and no block reads it." Both are true together: no `data` today, and `data` only under that binding once it is rendered. At the pin no renderer reads an element-level `provider: 'api'` binding: `core/src/data-scope/element-data-source.ts:169-176` (`isElementDataSourceConfig`) admits only a plain object with a non-empty string `object`, and the `provider: 'api'` readers at the pin are the view-level `ViewData` lane (`core/src/adapters/ApiDataSource.ts`, `resolveDataSource.ts`), not a page element's `dataSource`. The new pin ties the two texts: it goes red when `ElementApiDataSourceSchema`'s describe drops its `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` marker.
3. **`page:tabs` sentence — RIGHT.** FROM "`data` is surface-dependent: on a `page:tabs` item `visibleWhen` it is the record ROW instead" TO "A `page:tabs` item `visibleWhen` is a different evaluator: it binds `data` to the record ROW." `components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx:642-649` at the pin binds `data: recordData` and `record: recordData`, spreads the row's bare fields, and binds `current_user` and `page`. The word "instead", which implied a `data` on this surface as well, is gone.
4. **Unchanged clauses — RIGHT to leave.** "Visibility predicate (CEL) — component rendered only when TRUE", "Contract-bound roots: `record`, `current_user` (ADR-0068 aliases `user` / `ctx.user` — one object, three spellings), and page state as `page.VAR`", the "(ADR-0068 rules the user object only)" fence and the closing `e.g.` are byte-identical.
5. **Generated page — RIGHT.** The two `page.mdx` rows republish the describe verbatim; nothing else in that file moves.
6. **TSDoc face — RIGHT.** 「Ambient roots」 drops "and binds `data`"; the measurement line is re-pinned to `1fb1ced36243` with `ExpressionProvider.tsx:181-190` and `SchemaRenderer.tsx:665-676`, both verified; the new "No `data` root on this surface" section cites `SchemaRenderer.tsx:1194`, verified; "whose one shipping feeder, `ExpressionProvider`, publishes no `data`" holds (one production mount, item 1); the `page:tabs` section cites `containers.tsx:642-649`, verified. Dropping the `${data.total}` interpolation claim is right rather than a reword: `evaluateConfigBagInScope` (`SchemaRenderer.tsx:728-738`) builds from the same `configEvaluationScope`, so `data` resolves nowhere on this surface. The TSDoc's `objectui#9308` cite is a code comment, not a runtime string; the describe carries no tracker number.
7. **"Nothing an author can write changes" — TRUE.** The declaration is `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema.optional().describe(…)` at both the merge base (`:657`) and the head (`:678`); only the string moved. No key, enum, alias, strictness or union arm moves; `ElementApiDataSourceSchema` was already exported at the merge base (`:450`), so the new pin's import adds no export; no barrel changes; no wire shape. `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs` run in `Type Check · source gates`, success on this head.
8. **Still promised but not done — none found. Left unsaid that an AI author needs — none.** The describe names what to gate on instead (`record` for the row, `page.VAR` for state in the contract-bound clause) and the changeset gives the one-line fix. Two readings recorded rather than required: (a) "faults" is measured on the CEL envelope, which the describe scopes "(CEL)"; a bare-string predicate takes the legacy path, which the card did not measure; (b) `record` is bound only when the page has a row, which the TSDoc says and the describe's "the page's row is `record`" is consistent with.
9. **Residue at the head outside this diff, read for completeness.** Hand-written `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx:178` ("Binds `record`, `current_user`, and page state") and `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx` carry no `data` claim for this surface; `skills/**` none. The `component.zod.ts` twin is under ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23036-visiblewhen-no-data-root.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **patch**, its body carrying `Clause-②: no`; the PR body's second line is `Clause-②: no`; the claim 6136306937 declared `no`. **Right.** A describe-only correction in a released package is a fix, so `patch` is both the floor and the level; no accept set, export or wire shape moves (① item 7), so neither Clause-② arm applies and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. It is the declaration #17203 made for the `app` token, on the same reading: deleting an advertisement of a root that was never in the accept set narrows nothing an author can write. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report 6137432578 lists `open_questions: []`, two `dispatch_conflicts` and two `out_of_scope_findings`; the ACCEPT 6137462927 names four items. Each is answered:

- **A4, falsified — the correction stands.** The rule that answers a `data.`-rooted page-component predicate is `visibility-root-mislayered` at `warning` (`packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts:80-86`, emitted at `:1037-1046`), not `visibility-bare-identifier`: `data` is in `@objectstack/formula`'s `SCOPE_ROOTS` (`cel-engine.ts:131-156`), so the bare-identifier rule cannot fire on it. Its message (`:987`) already reads "on this runtime view/page surface it never matches and the element always renders", which is the new describe's claim. No lint change is owed by this card, and nothing in the diff depends on A4.
- **Affected-closure narrowing — accepted for this diff; CI's Test Core is the residual.** The dev ran the spec package's two vitest projects and 108 of 109 derived gate families (`check:type-check-debt` not measured, by order) and left the other 81 graph dependents to Test Core. The diff moves a `.describe()` string and TSDoc; a dependent's test can move only if it reads that string, and at the head no test outside `packages/spec` does (the `shape.visibleWhen` / describe readers outside spec are CHANGELOG entries and a comment in `packages/formula/src/validate.ts:126`). Test Core's conclusion is in the tally below; the landing's all-green precondition is the seat's pre-queue check, separate from this verdict.
- **`component.zod.ts:994-995` TSDoc twin, routed to #23103's PR as a declared rider — accepted as the seat's disposition, with an escalation condition.** The sentence "where the component-node evaluator binds it to the data-source ADAPTER" is false since ruling B, and the same docblock cites `containers.tsx:450-457` at pin `190fbd01d061` (the lines are `642-649` at `1fb1ced36243`). It is outside this PR's claimed file surface, so stopping at the fence was right. The published describe at `:1017` ("binds `data` to the record ROW (not the data-source adapter)") stays true of the `page:tabs` surface, but its parenthetical now contrasts against a binding the other surface no longer has, and it republishes into `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx:1564`; the rider's carrier should decide that parenthetical together with the TSDoc. #23103's PR is outside this record's input set, so the rider's presence there is not verified here. Escalation: if #23103's PR lands without the rider, a card is owed for `component.zod.ts:994-1006` plus the one-line TSDoc-face assertion in `expression-scope-data-root.pin.test.ts` the dev report drafted.
- **`validate-visibility-predicates.ts:343` comment kept in Acceptance notes — right.** It is a module docblock recording the measurement behind the bare-identifier union; its conclusion holds because `data` is in `SCOPE_ROOTS` either way, it reaches no author, and no gate asserts it (the objectui pin-citation gate checks pin-anchored citations; this one cites "objectui `main` at the time of #22212"). An acceptance note is what Prime Directive #10 asks for a non-defect; the next change to that file should correct the clause.
- **The two `dispatch_conflicts`** — the closure narrowing (above) and an attribution trailer amended before any push (a process note with no diff effect) — raise nothing further.

**Check-runs on the head, as read.** Read at 2026-10-13T03:35Z: 39 check-runs — 28 success, 5 skipped (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix shard, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 6 in progress (`Test Core` shards 2/6 to 6/6 and `Type Check · workspace`), 0 failure. Of the seven queue-required names: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is skipped by its path filter; `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` are aggregate jobs that report after their shards and lanes (`Type Check · source gates`, `consumer gates` and `debt ledger` are success; `workspace` is running) and had not yet reported. The PR is draft, `mergeable_state: blocked`, 280 changed lines, no governed path in its file list. This record does not wait on the running checks; their conclusions are the gate verdicts, and the seat reads them before the queue.
